anomalies.observed: In the 'MAIN PUMP & VALVE DRIVERS' block the ATO solenoid valve is switched by transistor T5, whose part/value field reads 'AON6407'. A second AON6407, T3, is placed in the 24 V input path inside the POWER TRAIN block as the reverse-polarity protection FET (with R7 33k and D3 12V).
anomalies.expected: The specification places the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch at T3 (AON6407), driven via R10/T4, and lists the r2 discrete-switch set as containing T5 = AO3400A (a smaller SOT-23 N-MOSFET), not a second AON6407. So either the ATO switch should be an AO3400A, or the ATO switch should carry the reference T3 rather than T5.

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives `ATO_VALVE` net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).
r2 drops to a smaller discrete-switch set (`T1`/`T4` BT3904 ×2, `T2` IRLR2905, `T3` AON6407, `T5` AO3400A ×1)
MAIN PUMP & VALVE DRIVERS — 'ATO Valve': R10 100Ω, R11 4k7, R12 10k, T4 BT3904, T5 AON6407 (sheet 1); POWER TRAIN — 'Reverse polarity protection': T3 AON6407, R7 33k, D3 12V (sheet 1)

anomalies.impact: The valve driver uses the wrong part (AON6407 instead of the specified AO3400A) and the input reverse-polarity FET occupies the reference the specification assigns to the ATO switch. At minimum this is a sourcing/assembly deviation (different device and package footprint from the specified AO3400A) and the switching section no longer matches the intended bill of materials; the valve function itself would likely still operate because both devices are N-channel MOSFETs.

parsed.summary: The drawing matches the specification for the power train, I2C/isolator, sensor and TMC2209 stepper sections, but the ATO solenoid-valve switch is drawn as T5/AON6407 whereas the specification puts the ATO valve switch at T3 (AON6407) and lists T5 as an AO3400A, so the discrete switching section deviates from the intended design.
